the self-injection process is a complex and multi-physics problem, where the laser power is not the only relevant parameter.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
self-injection is a function of the laser power and the plasma density.

we have measured the critical power for the onset of self-injection and the scaling of the electron charge with P/P{cr}. The results show that self-injection is not a threshold phenomenon but occurs over an interval in P/P{cr}.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the laser power required for efficient electron injection in a laser wake-field accelerator is significantly lower than the value predicted by a simple analytical model.
the critical power P_{crit} for self-injection is a function of the plasma density, and that the charge saturation level of the laser wakefield accelerator is proportional to P/P_{crit}.
